LESSON: WRITING 12.5.1 THE WRITING PROCESS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.5: Writing 12.5.1 The writing process

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 12.5.1 The writing process. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can a good dialogue be written?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the process of writing a dialogue
2. write a dialogue on a given topic correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 12.5.1 THE WRITING PROCESS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 12.5.1 The writing process helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 12.5.1 THE WRITING PROCESS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the process of writing a dialogue

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the process of writing a dialogue. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the process of writing a dialogue.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.5.1 The writing process”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the process of writing a dialogue. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a dialogue on a given topic correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to write a dialogue on a given topic correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a dialogue on a given topic correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.5.1 The writing process to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a dialogue on a given topic correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 12.5.1 The writing process is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.5.1 The writing process”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the process of writing a dialogue)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.5.1 The writing process to a partner. (skill: write a dialogue on a given topic correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 12.5.1 The writing process to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the process of writing a dialogue.
3. Practise this skill: write a dialogue on a given topic correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 12.5.1 The writing process from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 12.5.1 The writing process: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 12.5.1 The writing process?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can a good dialogue be written?
2. Why should one write a dialogue?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 12.5.1 The writing process means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the process of writing a dialogue.
5. Be able to: write a dialogue on a given topic correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
